To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
co adaptive training of the brain computer interface and the brain itself can lead to improved performance of a motor imagery based brain computer interface.
the use of co adaptive training during a 4 day motor imagery based brain computer interface (MI BCI) experiment resulted in improved performance of the subjects.
co adaptive training improves the performance of MI BCI users, and the performance of MI based BCIs can be improved by adapting the decoding algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new BCI system based on the analysis of EEG data.
the use of a BCI to control an external device.
the question of how the human brain and the machine learn together.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
co adaptive training is a promising technique for improving performance of MI BCI systems.
the co adaptive training approach is a promising method to enhance the performance of a MI based EEG BCI.
the co adaptive BCI approach can improve BCI performance, especially in the first days of a training session, by providing a better feedback signal and a more accurate classifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
co adaptive training is a promising approach for improving the performance of MI based BCIs, and should be further investigated in future studies.

the BCI paradigm is a suitable platform for investigating co adaptation between brain and machine, and that this co adaptation is likely to be useful in real world applications of BCIs.
